neighbours.label: ' more' in a 'by X more than (by) Y' weighing of two causes or factors (driven by fear more than reason; X, more than any other, …); quantity comparatives ('more books than') and 'rather than' stay low. The - pole of the unit is the second half of a correlative ('as well ⟦as⟧', 'sowohl … als ⟦auch⟧')
fire: The general won the battle through patience more than through courage.
The old bridge was saved by luck more than by careful planning.
Her decision to leave was guided by instinct more than logic.
The festival owes its charm to the setting more than to the music.
It was the weather, more than the long distance, that wore the riders down.
The treaty was shaped by exhaustion more than by any real goodwill.
The teacher, more than any textbook, made the children love geometry.
He kept the shop open out of loyalty more than out of any hope of profit.
quiet: The general won more battles than any other officer in the army.
The old bridge carries more traffic than the new tunnel beside it.
Her decision to leave was guided by instinct rather than logic.
The festival sold more tickets this year than ever before.
It was the weather and the long distance that wore the riders down.
The treaty was signed by more than forty countries in a single afternoon.
The teacher and the textbook made the children love geometry.
He kept the shop open for more than thirty years without a holiday.

notes: Card: ' more' x3 ('by his fear⟦ more⟧ than his reason', 'Baryshnikov,⟦ more⟧ than any other dancer'), ' más' x2, and an opening ' [' x3 for a bracketed insert, 'where appropriate', 'si se permite'. Probes: 'by sympathy more than evidence' 0.96, 'to trade more than to conquest' 0.64, ', more than his talent,' 0.43, ', more than by any king' 0.49, ', more than any other artist' 0.30, ' [n = 7]' 0.62; 'more books than anyone' 0.02, 'rather than' 0.05, 'if you will' 0.16, 'where appropriate' 0.08. Only the ' more' sense is tested; the bracket-insert sense is in the top examples but not in this test.
